# The reveal-pin screenshot baselines predate the inline-header trim, so DockPinCollapseNL is red on dev

## Problem

`test/playwright/e2e/dashboard/DockPinCollapseNL.spec.mjs` holds eight darwin baselines under `DockPinCollapseNL.spec.mjs-snapshots/reveal-pin-<theme>-{enabled,disabled}-chromium-darwin.png` (four themes × two states), asserting the reveal pin stays compact and legible per theme. #18048 (merged this morning) changed how the inline header renders — the title weight moved to the tab and the header trimmed — so the overlay header the arms screenshot no longer matches the stored images. The arms are red on plain `dev` for the baselines' reason, not the product's; the five-beat journey and the rest of the dock e2e suite pass (defect-noted on the A2A channel at 12:32Z).

## Evidence

- Snapshot directory: `test/playwright/e2e/dashboard/DockPinCollapseNL.spec.mjs-snapshots/` — eight `reveal-pin-*` files, all darwin.
- The screenshot arms: `DockPinCollapseNL.spec.mjs` at the `toHaveScreenshot` calls inside "the reveal pin is compact and legible under <theme>".
- The change that aged them out: #18048 (tab owns the title weight; inline header trimmed).

## Change

Re-record the eight baselines on darwin with the e2e config and the Brain runtime root (`--update-snapshots`), commit only the images, and confirm the spec is green against the new files twice. No product or spec-logic change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The eight `reveal-pin-*` darwin images are regenerated from current `dev`; the PR diff is images only.
- [ ] `DockPinCollapseNL.spec.mjs` passes twice in a row locally against the new baselines (e2e config, Brain root).
- [ ] The PR body names the head the images were recorded at.

## Non-goals

- Linux baselines (none exist for these arms; CI does not run the screenshot arms).
- Any change to the reveal header's rendering.

Sweep 13:14–13:19Z before filing: live latest-20 open (no match), A2A last-12 (no match), Knowledge Base (no leaf).
